text: We evaluated adaptive label smoothing weighted by per-sample loss drop (smoothing_max 0.3) in a weak-to-strong setting with qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, across 6 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.62 accuracy and the strong ceiling was 0.88, with the strong student trained on weak labels attaining a transfer accuracy of 0.66 (SE 0.03). The resulting performance gap recovered was 0.16 with a standard error of 0.12, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.06. Because the measured difference from the baseline falls well within two standard errors of the PGR estimate, these data do not support a claim that the method improves on the baseline; the direction is nominally favorable but indistinguishable from noise at this sample size. The large PGR standard error relative to its mean indicates substantial seed-to-seed variability, so any conclusion would require more seeds. No baseline standard error was reported, which further limits comparison.
